extracted.intended_audience: journal editors, peer reviewers, and authors (particularly those submitting to Eurosurveillance or similar biomedical journals)
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedures for handling submissions, conflicts of interest, expedited peer review, investigations of alleged misconduct, and decisions about retraction in a biomedical journal (Eurosurveillance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial board member submission policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Members of the Eurosurveillance editorial board may submit manuscripts to the journal, in keeping with the policies of many other respected scholarly journals. However, articles submitted by members of the board are not given any priority over other manuscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When editorial board members are authors of a submitted manuscript, they are not involved in any stage of the peer review or the editorial decision-making, nor do they have access to confidential information related to the decision-making process. Whether or not authors are members of the editorial board has no bearing on editorial consideration, nor any effect on the editorial evaluation or review processes (links provided). These principles were followed for the article by Corman et al.; the journal has rejected articles submitted by board members on many occasions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of conflicted editors from proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Associate editors who are co-authors on a manuscript are excluded from all related proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the case at hand, the two co-authors who were associate editors were excluded from all related proceedings. This exclusion was applied during the investigation of the retraction request to avoid involvement in decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential double-blind peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Eurosurveillance has a confidential peer review process and a policy of double-blind peer review, in which both the authors' and the reviewers' identities are confidential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer review reports are not made publicly available and are considered internal documents intended solely to guide editorial decision-making. Sharing reviewer reports with third parties would violate the assumed confidentiality obligations for journals that apply this peer review model, as per ICMJE and WAME recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review reports are internal and confidential
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review reports are internal documents intended solely to guide editorial decision-making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sharing reviewer reports with third parties would violate the assumed confidentiality obligations for journals that apply this peer review model, according to ICMJE and WAME. During investigations, internal documentation may be made available to non-conflicted associate editors to confirm process integrity, but public release of reports is not the norm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of expedited/fast-track review in exceptional situations
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions can be fast-tracked and reviewed rapidly when warranted by an exceptional and rapidly evolving public health situation and a need to enable timely action (e.g., enabling laboratories to detect a newly emerged virus).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expedited review may include a pre-submission enquiry, contacting potential peer reviewers to stand by, reviewers picking up assignments immediately, and authors standing by to respond quickly. The in-house editorial team's capacity can allow updates shortly before publication. The journal notes that expedited review does not necessarily affect the filtering function of peer review nor compromise reviewers' ability to critically assess content, validity and quality. Since 2015, about 30% of rapid communications were published less than 2 weeks following submission, including peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-submission enquiry and standby review workflow for rapid review
rubrics_metrics.description: For rapid consideration, editors may conduct a pre-submission enquiry and contact potential peer reviewers who agree to stand by to review the submission should it pass initial screening.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If fast-tracking, reviewers may be asked to pick up assignments immediately and submit verdicts within hours; authors may be asked to stand by to respond on short notice. All parties may work intensively, including outside usual hours, to finalize the submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review must be conducted in full by independent experts
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews should be conducted in full and by independent experts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Following allegations, associate editors (except conflicted co-authors) were given access to the full documentation of the evaluation and review process to confirm that the reviews were conducted in full and by independent experts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation of external subject experts for scientific-content allegations
rubrics_metrics.description: Allegations related to the scientific content of a paper should be assessed in consultation with external subject experts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The editorial team involved external subject experts to assess the allegations. In this case, a group of five laboratory experts reviewed the detailed allegations and provided comments that were made available to the associate editors (except conflicted co-authors).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of scientific adequacy relative to purpose and available data
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific adequacy of a methodological paper should be judged for its purpose and relative to the limited data and material available at the time of submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The consulted experts confirmed that the Corman et al. article was scientifically adequate for its purpose and for the limited data and material available at this early stage in the COVID-19 pandemic. The editorial team notes that with more data and evolving knowledge, laboratories and researchers may improve initial methods as per usual practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laboratory users must ascertain assay fitness and comply with local requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Any laboratory deciding to use published primers and protocols must ascertain the assay for its fitness for purpose and compliance with local quality and accreditation requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article provided an initial protocol that laboratories worldwide have since ascertained and improved; local validation and accreditation checks are expected before clinical or diagnostic use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retraction decisions require fulfillment of retraction criteria after investigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Retraction of an article requires that established criteria for retraction be fulfilled following a thorough investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After investigation and collection of scientific advice from various sources, including external reviewers, the editorial team unanimously (except for involved co-authors) decided that the criteria for a retraction of the article had not been fulfilled. The page implies that a formal assessment process—initial evaluation, editorial board discussion, external expert consultation—is appropriate before retracting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency to non-conflicted associate editors during investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: During inquiries into allegations, non-conflicted associate editors can be given access to full documentation of the evaluation and review process to enable confirmation of proper conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Following allegations, all associate editors—except the two co-authors who were associate editors—were given access to the full documentation so they could confirm reviews were conducted fully and by independent experts.
